Well, was she any good? That’s bound to be the first question anyone asks about this revival of Rodgers’ and Hammerstein’s masterpiece, starring glamour girl Katherine Jenkins in what appears to be her first professional theatrical role. The answer is yes.

For the third of its “semi-staged” musical revivals with the GradeLinnit Company (following Sweeney Todd and Sunset Boulevard), English National Opera takes a spin on Carousel, the Rodgers and Hammerstein 1945 classic. It’s a mixed ride.
But mostly, like the best types of fairground rides, this does not disappoint.
The 2¾-hour evening attempts to marry musical values with those of opera (with a sprinkling of ballet attractively choreographed by Josh Rhodes) and the results can be a little mixed.

cn.t: This ENO semi-staged revival of Rodgers and Hammerstein's masterpiece delivers swooning melodies and operatic grandeur, with Katherine Jenkins and Alfie Boe earning praise despite questions about their theatrical credentials.
